commands.command: design: ToolCallRuntime.invoke() enforces five real fail-closed bindings, all before any tool effect: capability (CapabilityAuthority.authorize(), never self-granted), purpose (GovernedContext.purpose, already fail-closed at the sealed kernel's own construction, revalidated here defensively), marking (MarkingEngine.require_authorized against the caller's real clearance), stop (EmergencyStopController.guard_dispatch's real epoch fence), and budget (TokenBudget.consume(), charged strictly before the tool is ever attempted). Only after all five pass does the real expression reach the sealed StrictSandbox for AST-whitelisted execution -- an escape-syntax attempt is refused there, before the registered tool function itself is ever called, exactly as the sealed sandbox already guaranteed. A successful call returns an immutable ToolCallReceipt; every denial path is proven, via a shared in-memory effects list appended to only by the real registered tool, to produce exactly zero tool effect.

requirement_results.command: a call passing all five bindings produces an immutable receipt and a real registered tool effect
a revoked lease, and a fabricated lease never issued by the authority, both produce zero tool effect
an escape-syntax attempt, and a call referencing a non-registered/forbidden-looking name, are both refused by the sealed sandbox's AST whitelist before the registered tool function is ever called
a call whose estimated token cost exceeds the remaining budget is refused before the sandbox is ever reached
a real clearance check via the sealed MarkingEngine refuses a call whose clearance does not dominate the content marking
the sealed GovernedContext itself fails closed on an empty purpose at construction, before this task's own code is ever reached
an active emergency stop, and a call fenced to a stale epoch after a stop/reset cycle, both produce zero tool effect via the sealed EmergencyStopController.guard_dispatch
one legitimate call plus four distinct denial scenarios run in sequence against a shared effects list produce exactly one real effect
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This task builds the smallest contract-compliant slice of the five-way tool boundary as standalone, composable gates; it does not itself wire ToolCallRuntime into AgentKernel.invoke() or AgentRunOrchestrator's own lifecycle (OCOR-DEV-0046) -- a future integration task would compose all three, the same way OCOR-DEV-0043's HumanGateCoordinator composes into GovernedActionEngine.execute without engine.py itself changing.

The budget charge for a call that fails at the sandbox stage (an escape-syntax attempt) is not refunded, matching real-world model-API billing semantics (a real resource cost was incurred attempting the call, even though the tool itself never ran) -- an explicit, deliberate design choice, not an oversight.

estimated_tokens is a caller-supplied upfront estimate charged via TokenBudget.consume() rather than a reserve/commit pair, since a deterministic tool call (unlike a model generating variable-length output) has a known cost at call time; a future tool with genuinely variable cost would need the reserve/commit pattern AgentKernel.invoke() already establishes.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
rollback_procedure_verified: tool_runtime.py is additive only (a new file in the existing c8/ package, no existing sealed file modified); reverting is a plain file deletion plus removal of its extension_paths/evidence entries, with zero change to c8_agent.py, c8/orchestrator.py, c6_capabilities.py, c4_marking.py, c6/safety.py or kernel/governed_context.py.
